title: What The Harp Knows (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 100bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal music philosophy absurdist Zimbabwe family harp
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The harp has forty-seven strings and seven pedals and the whole
Concert takes an hour to tune before it plays its role
The harpist arrives early and tunes for the full hour
And then plays something so beautiful it unmakes your power

[Pre-Chorus]
The harp is the instrument most associated with heaven
Which places it at both extremes of any given seven
On the emotion scale — weddings and funerals claim it equally
And the harp doesn't distinguish between them sequentially

[Chorus]
What does the harp know that I don't know?
It knows that forty-seven strings and seven pedals run the show
What does the harp know when it opens up its sound?
It knows that whatever's above us and whatever's underground
Is listening — that's my boy

[Verse 2]
The glissando is the harp's particular signature move
One sweep across all forty-seven strings in the groove
Of the moment and the sound is the sound of something giving
A summary of everything — and then the harp keeps living

[Bridge]
My mother had a harp she couldn't play in the corner of the room
In Zimbabwe — and it sat there in the particular perfume
Of potential — the potential to be something when the fingers learned
Which they didn't — but the harp was patient and it never turned

[Outro]
Harp knows… forty-seven strings and perfect patience… harp knows
That's my boy
